author: WP02
summary: An alpha.1-era chapter on why CNA keeps three static-archive cycles, its umbrella targets, narrow aliases, the minimal-link module probes and their negative contracts, the Ninja caveat, include reachability and header self-containment, the partition guards and a safe boundary-change procedure. At TARGET there are fifteen probes, the build-flags target is cna_build_config, the HEADLESS and Vulkan closures require single-renderer mode, and the reachability and self-containment scripts are stale and unwired. The Development pages had the edges and a short Ninja note; the reasoning, the per-probe contracts, the CI reality and the violation symptoms went into a new boundaries deep dive.

concepts.text: A dependency cycle can be an architecture defect, a static-linking fact or a faithful expression of the framework's semantics, so a graph with every cycle removed is not the goal.

target.evidence: modules/graphics, input, audio, media CMakeLists.txt (cycle comments)

concepts.text: The goal is to declare every required edge, keep public closures no wider than necessary and make accidental edges fail mechanically.
CNA declares three cycles on both members so that CMake repeats the static archives on the final link line.
tokens: declares three cycles on both of their members

concepts.text: Graphics and input: GraphicsDevice updates TouchPanel display metrics and binds Mouse and TextInput to a window, while MouseCursor is built from a Texture2D.
Audio and media: FrameworkDispatcher pumps MediaPlayer, and media playback submits songs through the audio mixer.

Graphics and the selected renderer: graphics constructs the renderer through the family's factory, and every renderer implements the graphics-owned contract whose header-inlined defaults call back into core logging.
concepts.note: At TARGET every compiled family, not only one selected renderer, has the edge.

concepts.text: The first two cycles come from XNA-shaped ownership; moving MouseCursor or the dispatcher could trade the cycle for a new abstraction, but deleting an edge without relocating the semantic owner only creates unresolved symbols or a missing update path.
tokens: deleting an edge without relocating the semantic owner

concepts.text: FrameworkDispatcher lives in the audio module because ownership follows dependency direction; putting it in runtime would create a runtime-to-audio cycle, and its touch-panel edge to input is declared directly rather than inherited through media.
The renderer cycle is a compile-time composition seam: CNA does not load a renderer plug-in after start-up.
tokens: does not load a renderer plug-in

concepts.text: Graphics and input set LINK_INTERFACE_MULTIPLICITY 3 because the Direct3D helper archive makes the cycle three archives deep; a real Direct3D 12 test link failed with two repetitions.
When a static link fails, inspect the generated final link line before adding a PUBLIC dependency; repeating two intended archives is different from making every module link the whole umbrella.
tokens: inspect the generated final link line before adding a new PUBLIC dependency

target.evidence: general CMake static-archive semantics as used by the module files

concepts.text: CNA is the historical full-framework INTERFACE target carrying runtime, framework modules, the extension modules, the build configuration and the default renderer; existing games keep linking it, and Design, Phone, Inspector, the pipeline, GamerServices and Net stay outside.
concepts.note: Exclusions and diagnostics/platform membership made explicit.

concepts.text: With CNA_SHARED_LIBRARY the umbrella is re-pointed at libcna.so and every compiled renderer family is named, because tests call renderer internals.
cna_cnaext / CNA::CnaExt composes CNA::GraphicsExt and CNA::DevicesExt; it is neither the CNAEXT declaration marker nor a renderer.

The Bible's definitions-only cna_build_flags / CNA::BuildFlags is cna_build_config / CNA::BuildConfig at TARGET: it carries the C++23 feature, the default renderer macro and feature definitions (and Emscripten ABI link options) and exports no include directory.

Removing the global include root closed a loophole: declarations reached accidentally through common flags now fail unless the declaring module is reachable, as MediaPlayer's TouchPanel include showed.

concepts.section: Narrow aliases are the architectural surface
concepts.text: A subsystem test or reusable library should link the narrowest alias whose surface it uses; a game may use CNA, a math-only helper CNA::Math, a content tool should state what it needs.

concepts.section: Narrow aliases are the architectural surface
concepts.text: PUBLIC and PRIVATE are CMake propagation: content's public headers expose graphics, audio and media types so those edges are PUBLIC; its cgltf/stb include roots, zstd and Draco are private, and at TARGET content links no SDL.
tokens: at this snapshot it links no SDL at all
concepts.note: The Bible lists SDL among content's private needs.

concepts.section: Narrow aliases are the architectural surface
concepts.text: A consumer that compiles only because a private third-party include leaked from its environment has no supported contract.

target.evidence: PRIVATE include roots in module CMake files

concepts.section: Narrow aliases are the architectural surface
concepts.text: The audio module links its backend libraries privately and only for the selected CNA_AUDIO_PLATFORM, so an SDL2-only binary cannot keep an SDL3 link through cna_audio.

On native test configurations CNA registers one small consumer per composition boundary; the Bible's fourteen (Math, Core, Graphics, Content, Runtime, Input, Audio, Media, Storage, Devices, DevicesExt, GraphicsExt, CnaExt, Net) are fifteen at TARGET with Design.

Each probe yields ModuleProbe_<name> (build and run the consumer) and ModuleLinkClosure_<name> (inspect the link line for required and forbidden libraries); the registered names carry the probe_ prefix.
A closure test is registered only when Python 3 is found and the probe has a forbid pattern; the CnaExt probe is checked by a separate composition gate.
tokens: registered only when a Python 3 interpreter is found

concepts.text: The forbid expressions encode each module's contract, for example Math forbids every CNA archive but its own plus SDL3, ENet, FFmpeg and renderers, and Runtime forbids devices, extensions, storage and networking.

The probes are excluded on Emscripten and Android; that is a host boundary of link inspection, not evidence that the graph differs, and platform claims must say whether they are source-validated, cross-compiled or link-inspected.
Storage's closure forbids every libcna_ archive except libcna_storage, even libcna_core; PlayerIndex, the CNAEXT marker and path containment arrive through CNA::CoreHeaders.

DevicesExt encodes that project-owned CNA::Devices services never depend on the XNA-shaped Microsoft::Devices module; its regex escapes the dot after libcna_devices so it rejects the base archive without matching the extension archive itself.
These negative assertions are more informative than an umbrella consumer, which would succeed regardless of accidental edges.
tokens: say more than an umbrella consumer could

concepts.text: Additional gates require ENet for Net and both extension libraries for CnaExt, isolate the Vulkan SDK from other renderer SDKs and keep HEADLESS free of native graphics SDKs; at TARGET the HEADLESS and Vulkan closures exist only in single-renderer trees.
concepts.note: Single-renderer condition added (a multi build defaulting to HEADLESS legitimately links other SDKs).

concepts.text: The core probe does not forbid libSDL3 and still comments that SDL3 is a private detail of the core logger, although core no longer includes SDL; an SDL link returning to core would not fail it.
tokens: The core probe does not forbid

concepts.text: With CNA_DEVICES OFF the DevicesExt probe uses no extension symbol, so only the declared link closure is checked, not that the extension code links.
tokens: only the declared link closure is checked

concepts.section: The Ninja caveat: registered does not mean executed
concepts.text: The closure checker reads CMakeFiles/<target>.dir/link.txt, which Makefiles generators write and Ninja does not; without it the script exits 77 and SKIP_RETURN_CODE 77 makes CTest report skipped.

concepts.section: The Ninja caveat: registered does not mean executed
concepts.text: The test preset and CI use Ninja, so the closure entries are registered but inspect nothing; at TARGET the only unfiltered ctest workflow (general-tests-ci) configures with -G Ninja, and the Makefiles-default devices and Apple lanes do not run these tests, so no workflow evaluates a closure contract.
tokens: By reading, no workflow evaluates a link-closure contract
concepts.note: The Bible says 'hosted workflows use Ninja'; some use Makefiles but never run the gates.

concepts.section: The Ninja caveat: registered does not mean executed
concepts.text: A minimal consumer that compiles, and other validators that pass, do not close the negative-link claim.
tokens: Only the third and fourth are evidence about the boundary itself

concepts.section: The Ninja caveat: registered does not mean executed
concepts.text: A report must separate: probe compiled and ran; closure test registered; closure inspected a real link line under a compatible generator; a forbidden-library mutation was shown to fail.
tokens: a deliberate forbidden-library mutation was shown to fail the gate

concepts.section: The Ninja caveat: registered does not mean executed
concepts.text: Test presence, execution and oracle engagement are separate coordinates of evidence.

concepts.section: The Ninja caveat: registered does not mean executed
concepts.text: The checker is passed CMAKE_BINARY_DIR, so in a tree where CNA is a subproject it looks in the consumer's root and skips.

concepts.section: The Ninja caveat: registered does not mean executed
concepts.text: The Wayland link-closure test reads the dynamic section of the linked binaries and so does not depend on the generator.
Include reachability resolves public CNA and Microsoft headers through the declared module graph and attributes renderer-gated includes to the selected family.
concepts.note: The tool exists but is a stale campaign tool at TARGET (see the next concepts).

concepts.text: Header self-containment asks whether each public header compiles with only its documented prerequisites instead of relying on include order.

These checks answer different questions from the linker probes: a declaration can be reachable while its library is absent, and a link can succeed through a broad umbrella while a header needs another include first; a healthy boundary needs compile and link evidence.
tokens: A healthy boundary needs both compile and link evidence

target.evidence: reasoning about the two tools and the probes

concepts.text: At TARGET both scripts hard-code the August 2026 graph (fourteen modules, a pre-curation renderer map) and no CMake file, CTest registration, workflow or script runs them; by reading, their table would flag runtime, graphics, input and audio includes of CNA/Platform headers.

target.evidence: modularization/tools/check_include_reachability.py (PUBLIC table); grep of cmake, workflows, scripts

concepts.note: The Bible presents them as active checks; WP02-i003.

concepts.text: What runs today is narrower: ContractIsSdlFreeTests compiles all platform contract headers together, CApiHeaderCompatibility compiles each C header alone, and no gate compiles each public C++ header in isolation.
tokens: No current gate compiles each public C++ header

concepts.text: The partition validator and the legacy-root guard prevent two regressions: a new TU outside every owner picked up by an ad hoc glob, and a global include root quietly restoring reachability.
tokens: Every translation unit has a physical owner
No global include or source root

concepts.text: The renderer identity validator keeps CMake's accepted names and the C++ enum the same set; at TARGET it also covers the registry map, the C ABI values, each identity's descriptor accessor and stated counts, and it cannot prove behaviour.
tokens: follows each identity through to the descriptor accessor

concepts.text: Other boundary gates at TARGET: ContractIsSdlFreeTests (#error on SDL/Vulkan/GL sentinels), the SDL ratchet, non-production audit and hot-path lint, CnaWaylandLinkClosure, the renderer discipline scripts, the descriptor gate and the preset build-performance policy.

concepts.section: How to change a boundary safely
concepts.text: A boundary change is complete only when the file moves to its owner, edges are updated, reachability and header isolation are checked, a probe is added or narrowed, a real link artifact is inspected, a negative mutation fails, and examples, tests and citations are updated; at TARGET the reachability step is manual and the link inspection needs a Makefiles tree.
concepts.note: Steps adapted to the stale tools and the generator requirement.

concepts.section: How to change a boundary safely
concepts.text: An umbrella build going green is the beginning of the argument about a boundary, not its conclusion.
tokens: An umbrella build going green is the beginning of that argument

concepts.section: How to change a boundary safely
concepts.text: What violations look like: the partition and legacy-root FATAL_ERROR texts, 'FORBIDDEN link inputs for probe_<name>' or 'MISSING required link input', the platform contract #error, and an undefined reference at the final link when a cycle edge is removed.

issues.text: No workflow evaluates a ModuleLinkClosure_* contract: the only unfiltered ctest job uses Ninja, where the checker skips (77).
probe_core does not forbid libSDL3 and carries a stale comment about SDL in core's logger.
check_include_reachability.py and check_header_self_containment.py hard-code a pre-TARGET graph and are not run anywhere.
check_module_link_closure is passed CMAKE_BINARY_DIR; in a subproject tree it looks in the wrong directory and always skips.
No gate compiles each public C++ header of the framework modules in isolation.
